## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The change to `requirement_proven` makes it treat an empty criteria list as proven. This needs fixing before merge because a requirement with no evidence would now be reported as satisfied.

## Changes
The pull request rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a sum of `proven` flags against the criteria count. It also adds `reviewed_batch`, which rejects empty batches, and adds `tests/test_proof.py` to cover both functions.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — Return False for empty criteria in requirement_proven — `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True`, because `sum(...)` of nothing is `0` and that equals `len([])`. The base version returned `False` through `bool(criteria) and ...`. — Requirements with no criteria are reported as proven, so unproven requirements show a passing proof status. — Fix: restore the emptiness guard, `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, and extend `test_requirement_with_evidence` with an empty-list case.

## Important
- app/proof.py:2 — correctness — Count truthy proven flags instead of summing them — If a `proven` value is a non-boolean, `sum` gives the wrong result: `[{"proven": 2}, {"proven": 0}]` returns `True`, and a string value such as `"yes"` raises `TypeError`. The base `all(...)` handled both cases by truthiness. — Any criterion that stores a count or string marks a partly proven requirement as proven, or crashes the status check. — Fix: use `all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, which also fixes the empty-list case together with the guard above.
